mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 5% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points, sustained for two months, indicates a tightening labor market that increases wage pressures and input costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by >0.3pp for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly different from zero at 10% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in real GDP growth below 1% for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 1% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 5% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index of more than 0.5% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >0.5% in a month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 10% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the Housing Starts Index and Real Personal Income above their prior three-month average signals stronger household demand, which boosts consumption-sensitive sectors and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise above 3-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly above zero at 5% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both payroll employment and unemployment rate above their prior month values indicates a compositional shift toward lower-wage jobs, which reduces average labor productivity and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises and UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 10% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held constant at or below 0.5% for six consecutive months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS <= 0.5% for six consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly above zero at 5% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly real GDP growth acceleration from negative to above 3% signals a cyclical upturn in aggregate demand, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 transitions from negative to >3% annualized growth between two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered quarters, or the median return is not significantly above zero at 5% confidence.
